question: Examine whether the vectors $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=-4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-6\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=6\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+9\hat{k}$ are collinear. Also compare their directions.
explanation:
Step 1: Relationship between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$
Each component of $\vec{b}$ is $-2$ times the corresponding component of $\vec{a}$. Therefore,
\(\vec{b}=-2\vec{a}\)
Step 2: Relationship between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$
Each component of $\vec{c}$ is $3$ times the corresponding component of $\vec{a}$. Thus,
\(\vec{c}=3\vec{a}\)
Step 3: Collinearity conclusion
Since $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are scalar multiples of $\vec{a}$, all three vectors are collinear.
Step 4: Comparison of directions
The negative multiplier shows that $\vec{b}$ is opposite to $\vec{a}$. The positive multiplier shows that $\vec{c}$ has the same direction as $\vec{a}$.
Final Answer
The three vectors are collinear; $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ have the same direction, while $\vec{b}$ has the opposite direction.

options.A: $\vec{b}=-2\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}=3\vec{a}$; hence all three vectors are collinear. $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ have the same direction, while $\vec{b}$ has the opposite direction.
options.B: $\vec{b}=2\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}=3\vec{a}$; hence all three vectors have the same direction.
options.C: $\vec{b}=-2\vec{a}$ but $\vec{c}$ is not a scalar multiple of $\vec{a}$; hence the three vectors are not collinear.
options.D: $\vec{b}=2\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}=-3\vec{a}$; hence $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ have the same direction while $\vec{c}$ is opposite.
